item.title: Asian Games | China sweeps men's 10m air rifle golds with team world record
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- China claimed both the men's 10m air rifle individual and team gold medals at the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games on Monday, setting a world record in the team event. Zhang Changhong, Sheng Lihao and Ma Sihan all produced steady performances in qualification, with each finishing in the top eight. The trio combined for 1,899.0 points to take team gold, breaking the previous world record of 1,898.4. India won silver with 1,890.1 points, while South Korea claimed bronze with 1,884.2. The Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games marked 18-year-old Ma's first appearance at the continental event. With both of his teammates Olympic champions, Ma said he had learned a lot from them during preparations for the Games. "I feel like I have two great teammates to lean on, so I wasn't that nervous," Ma said. In the individual final, Sheng was locked in a close battle with India's Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil and Himanshu Dhillon. Patil scored 106.0 points after the first 10 shots to lead Sheng by 1.1 points. In the elimination stage, Sheng remained consistent, with only one shot below 10.5. Patil and Dhillon, meanwhile, registered lows of 9.8 and 9.7 respectively, and Sheng eventually won by 1.8 points. Sheng took individual gold with 254.2 points, improving his own Asian and Asian Games records and finishing just 0.8 points short of the world record. Dhillon took silver with 252.4 points, while Patil claimed bronze with 230.9. Ma finished fifth. The two titles on Monday took Sheng's Asian Games gold-medal tally to four. At the Hangzhou Asian Games, he won gold in the men's 10m air rifle individual and mixed team events. ■

item.title: Asian Games | Day 2: Yu, 13, sets swimming Asian record, Thai shuttler suspended for doping
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
by sportswriter Li Jia NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese teenager Yu Zidi's sensational Asian record propelled China's gold-medal charge on day two of the 2026 Asian Games on Monday, while Thai badminton player Pitchamon Opatniputh became the first known doping case of the Games. Pitchamon, 19, tested positive for the banned substance furosemide and was provisionally suspended. The International Testing Agency said an out-of-competition sample collected from Opatniputh in Nagoya on September 17 returned an Adverse Analytical Finding for furosemide. The substance is listed by the World Anti-Doping Agency as a specified substance prohibited at all times under the category of diuretics and masking agents. China claimed two shooting golds, including a world record, and five swimming titles, while Zhang Boheng won the men's gymnastics all-around gold to round off another prolific day for the delegation. In the pool, 13-year-old Yu maintained her stunning form. She came from behind to win the women's 200-meter individual medley in an Asian record of 2 minutes, 6.10 seconds, with teammate and defending champion Yu Yiting second in 2:07.99. Japan's Mio Narita took bronze in 2:10.40. Yu's winning time was just 0.40 seconds off the world record set by Canada's Summer McIntosh. "I feel even happier winning this second gold medal than I did with the first one," Yu said. Her performance produced the first Asian swimming record of the Games. Yu made her Asian Games debut by winning the 200 butterfly on Sunday. The excitement peaked in the men's 4x200 freestyle relay. Japan led for the first 750 meters as China stayed close behind. Pan Zhanle narrowed the gap on the third leg before Zhang Zhanshuo took the lead in the closing stages to give China gold in an Asian record of 7:00.17. Japan took silver in 7:01.05, while South Korea claimed bronze in 7:06.76. Adding to China's swimming success, backstroke specialist Xu Jiayu successfully defended his men's 50 backstroke title in a Games-record 24.04, while Wan Letian and Wang Xue'er finished 1-2 in the women's 50 backstroke. China's Dong Zhihao and Japan's Shin Ohashi shared gold in the men's 100 breaststroke in 58.64, while defending champion Qin Haiyang took bronze. South Korea claimed its first swimming gold of the Games as Kim Yeong-beom won the men's 50 freestyle, while defending champion Siobhan Haughey of Hong Kong, China took the women's 200 freestyle title. In shooting, China swept the men's 10-meter air rifle individual and team gold medals, setting a world record in the team event. The trio of Zhang Changhong, Sheng Lihao and Ma Sihan combined for 1,899.0 points to take team gold, breaking the previous world record of 1,898.4. India won silver with 1,890.1, while South Korea claimed bronze with 1,884.2. In gymnastics, China's Zhang Boheng retained the men's all-around title. Fresh from winning the same event at the Asian championships, the 26-year-old scored 85.065 points to take gold, while Japan's reigning Olympic champion Shinnosuke Oka and 2021 Olympic champion Daiki Hashimoto finished second and third, respectively. Zhang had finished runner-up to Oka at the Paris Olympics and to Hashimoto at last year's World Championships. "Gymnastics keeps progressing, and both Japanese all-around gymnasts have very high levels of difficulty and execution," Zhang said. China's success extended to other disciplines, with Lin Xinyu, Li Mingxu, Huang Anqi and Zhang Xirui winning the triathlon mixed relay in 1:25:54. Gong Li and Li Qiaoqiao added karate gold medals in the women's kumite 61-kilogram and 68-kilogram categories, respectively. In team sports, China's women's football team thrashed the Philippines 5-1 in Group G, while the women's volleyball team edged Thailand 3-2 to avenge its defeat in last month's Asian Championship final and advanced to the gold-medal match. China's women's basketball team beat Indonesia 110-41 in Group A. After two days of competition, China led the medal table with 23 gold, 10 silver and five bronze medals. Japan was second with eight gold, 12 silver and 12 bronze, followed by South Korea with five gold, 13 silver and 15 bronze. ■

item.title: Fast, focused and forward-looking, China's manufacturing opens new frontier
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
* Chinese manufacturers are taking a more targeted approach to global markets, moving beyond standardized products to create solutions tailored to specific needs in different global markets. * Stronger R&D capabilities and faster responses to market needs are allowing Chinese manufacturers to play a bigger role in product design and development. * From robotics and embodied intelligence to quantum computing, new applications are opening up a wide range of possibilities for manufacturing and creating new links with markets around the world. HEFEI, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- As Europe was gripped by extreme heat this summer, a production base in Wuhu City, east China's Anhui Province, was racing to meet urgent orders from its European clients: 20,000 mobile air conditioners had to be produced and loaded in just seven days. The tight deadline set an equally demanding task for the supply chain. More than 1,000 types of components had to be coordinated at the same time, with some rushed to the production line by air and high-speed rail to keep everything on schedule. Once completed, the air conditioners were transported overland across Eurasia to France. The seven-day turnaround was made possible by a manufacturing system built for rapid shifts in demand -- from adjusting production lines to coordinating suppliers and logistics in real time. Wuhu is just one part of Anhui's manufacturing landscape. Across the province, manufacturing runs at a scale that can be measured by the minute. "Every minute, about 190 home appliances, 50 laptops and four new energy vehicles roll off production lines across the province," said Liang Yanshun, Party chief of Anhui, at the ongoing World Manufacturing Convention in Hefei, the provincial capital. Increasingly, Chinese manufacturers are taking a more targeted approach to global markets, moving beyond standardized products to create solutions tailored to specific needs in different global markets. TARGETED SOLUTION In late March, Wuhu-based Tri Waters New Energy Technology Co., Ltd. signed a strategic cooperation agreement with the Maldives' transport authorities to export 32 electric sightseeing boats, each capable of carrying 100 passengers. Taking into account the Maldives' island geography and demand for greener transport, further plans are in the pipeline to build a photovoltaic energy storage system, charging and battery-swapping networks, and a vessel maintenance base. "This is a green mobility solution tailored to the Maldives," said Liu Yang, deputy general manager of the company, who noted that the Maldivian side had discussed and planned with the company before reaching a final deal. "The shift from simply 'taking orders' to 'solving problems' reflects a profound restructuring of the logic of global industrial division of labor," said Han Junhui, an associate researcher at the Chinese Academy of Science and Technology for Development. For decades, Chinese manufacturers have been engaged in global production networks primarily because of their strong industrial base and cost efficiency, often making products designed by overseas brands, Han said. "Now, stronger R&D capabilities and faster responses to market needs are allowing Chinese manufacturers to play a bigger role in product design and development," he added. FORWARD-LOOKING TECH The same shift is also visible in emerging sectors, where new technologies are still taking shape. From robotics and embodied intelligence to quantum computing, new applications are opening up a wide range of possibilities for manufacturing and creating new links with markets around the world. At the robotics and embodied intelligence exhibition area of the 2026 World Manufacturing Convention, nearly 200 robots are on display, showcasing applications in logistics, elderly care, services and other fields. Data from the General Administration of Customs of China show that China exported more than 12 million robots of various types in the first half of this year, with exports valued at 24.85 billion yuan (about 3.68 billion U.S. dollars), reaching more than 160 countries and regions. "China has a rich range of application scenarios and a strong manufacturing base. The rapid development of artificial intelligence has further strengthened the competitiveness of Chinese-made robots in international markets," said You Wei, chairman and general manager of EFORT Intelligent Robot Co., Ltd., a robotics manufacturer exhibiting at the conference. Guo Guangcan, an academician of the Chinese Academy of Sciences, said quantum technology worldwide has accelerated its transition from laboratory research to engineering validation, real-world applications and commercial deployment at scale. Hefei has now developed a complete technological system covering quantum chips, cryogenic cooling, measurement and control systems, operating software and cloud services, Guo noted. Through a quantum computing cloud platform open to users worldwide, its computing services have reached 192 countries and regions, with more than 55 million visits and over 1.16 million scientific research and industrial computing tasks completed. "These applications have demonstrated the feasibility of commercializing quantum computing at scale and provided a practical path for the global open sharing and cross-sector application of quantum technologies," Guo said. ■

item.title: Xiplomacy: Five years on, China's Global Development Initiative delivers tangible progress
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
by Xinhua writers Liu Bowei, He Yixuan BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- "Stay committed to putting development first, and open up the prospects for shared prosperity." At the Shanghai Cooperation Organization (SCO) summit in Bishkek this year, Chinese President Xi Jinping once again called on countries to make development a priority. In September 2021, Xi proposed the Global Development Initiative (GDI) at the 76th session of the UN General Assembly, bringing a vision of shared development to the global agenda and calling for the benefits of development to be more widely shared. Five years on, the initiative has evolved from a vision into concrete cooperation, with more and more countries joining forces in the pursuit of a better future for all. FROM VISION TO SHARED ASPIRATION The GDI was put forward at a critical moment when the global development agenda was facing unprecedented challenges. In the Sustainable Development Goals Report 2021, the United Nations underscored the scale of the setback: global extreme poverty rose for the first time in more than 20 years, with 119 million to 124 million people pushed back into extreme poverty in 2020, while 101 million children fell below the minimum reading proficiency level. It was against this background that Xi proposed the development initiative, emphasizing the necessity to put development high on the global macro policy agenda. The initiative calls for staying committed to development as a priority, to a people-centered approach, to benefits for all, to innovation-driven development, to harmony between man and nature and to results-oriented actions. "It was both timely and strategically far-sighted. At a time when the international agenda is increasingly dominated by differences and dividing lines, the initiative brings a fundamental question back into focus: how to achieve development and stability and create a dignified future for people," said Serik Korzhumbayev, editor-in-chief of the Delovoy Kazakhstan newspaper. In January 2022, when the Group of Friends of the GDI was launched at the UN Headquarters in New York, delegates from more than 100 countries attended the meeting, voicing support for the initiative and willingness to join the group. "Development holds the key to people's well-being." Over the past five years, Xi has continued to promote the implementation of the initiative at the SCO, BRICS, the Forum on China-Africa Cooperation, the G20 and other multilateral platforms, calling for building political consensus to ensure everyone values development and all countries pursue cooperation together. "This is where I see particular value in the GDI: it links development with people, and national needs with the shared responsibility of the international community," Essam Sharaf, former Egyptian prime minister and founder and chairman of the Sharaf Foundation for Sustainable Development, told Xinhua. As of now, nearly 100 countries and international and regional organizations have signed cooperation documents with China on the initiative, while the Group of Friends of the GDI has grown to 88 countries. Reflecting on the GDI's progress over the past five years, Abdulaziz Alshaabani, a Saudi researcher at the Al Riyadh Center for Political and Strategic Studies, said the initiative "has evolved from a Chinese proposal into concrete mechanisms for international cooperation." "One noticeable change since the launch of the GDI is that more and more countries have begun to place development and related issues higher on the international cooperation agenda," said Alshaabani. PROGRESS IN ACTION In Rwinkwavu, a rural area in Kayonza district of Rwanda's drought-prone Eastern Province, a bank of solar panels enclosed by a blue fence stand among the hills. The solar-powered borehole is one of 200 drilled under a China-funded project benefiting about 110,000 people across the province. Magnifique Habimana, head teacher of GS Rwinkwavu school, one of the beneficiaries, told Xinhua that "the project came at the right time to address a serious water problem." Over the past five years, stories like this have unfolded in communities across the developing world. While projects involving infrastructure, energy and water have made everyday life easier, agricultural cooperation has expanded to more than 140 countries and regions, with over 1,000 agricultural technologies shared with developing countries and more than 14,000 technicians trained in hybrid rice technology. "For developing countries, development is not an abstract political formula. It means new roads and railways, reliable energy supplies, modern enterprises, jobs, education, digital connectivity, food security, access to technology and better prospects for the younger generation," Korzhumbayev told Xinhua. Backed by more than 23 billion U.S. dollars in funds it has mobilized, the initiative has implemented over 1,800 "small and beautiful" projects and trained more than 200,000 professionals, delivering concrete benefits to local communities in over 120 countries. At the SCO Bishkek Summit, Xi announced plans to implement 100 technological cooperation projects with other SCO countries in the next three years and nurture more green industry talents through China-SCO cooperation, building on his pledge a year earlier at the SCO Tianjin Summit that "China plans to implement 100 'small and beautiful' livelihood projects in member states with such need." A defining feature of the GDI is its emphasis on action and tangible results, said Hussein Askary, vice-chairman of the Belt and Road Institute in Sweden. "China not only discusses development issues, but also takes concrete action to advance common development." A PATH FORWARD Five years on, development remains as an urgent priority as ever, as geopolitical conflicts, economic uncertainty and climate change compound the pressing challenges facing the international community. The latest UN data show that only 36 percent of the Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) targets with available trend data are on track or making moderate progress, and 15 percent have even regressed below their 2015 baselines. "This is precisely why, in my view, the significance of the GDI has actually increased over the past five years," said Emin Gasimov, director of Azerbaijan's Center for the Study of China's Global Initiatives, Development and Culture. While emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence (AI), are creating new development opportunities, they also pose a risk of widening existing gaps. Sharaf noted that the GDI presents a major opportunity to help shape an important principle for the next phase. "The future of technology should not be a future for a limited number of countries, but a shared future for humanity," he said. Xi has described AI as "a new engine of world economic growth and an accelerator for the shift of growth drivers." As a new round of technological revolution and industrial transformation gathers pace, he has called for bridging the digital and AI divides, so that technological revolution and development achievements can benefit all nations. In July, during the 2026 World Artificial Intelligence Conference (WAIC) and High-Level Meeting on Global AI Governance in Shanghai, an upgraded version of MAZU was officially handed over to Djibouti, marking a new step in China-Djibouti cooperation on AI-powered climate resilience. MAZU, short for multi-hazard, alert, zero-gap and universal, is an AI-driven meteorological early warning platform developed by China and named after the Chinese guardian goddess of the sea. Currently, MAZU has been deployed on the ground in seven countries and is providing cloud-based services in more than 40 countries, making it an important international public good serving countries across the Global South. At the 2026 WAIC, Xi announced that China will provide developing countries with 5,000 opportunities in AI training and seminar programs in the next five years, and said that 30 countries can use the AI-powered meteorological warning system to safeguard homes around the world. Projects such as MAZU offer a stellar example of how digital technologies can support the implementation of the GDI, said Alshaabani. "Its value lies not simply in providing a technology, but in helping countries strengthen their capacity for disaster early warning, risk management and emergency response." Beyond MAZU, China has been building a broader framework for international AI cooperation, including establishing the World AI Cooperation Organization with 28 other countries and setting up international AI application cooperation centers with major regional and multilateral organizations. If such emerging technologies can be made more accessible to the Global South, the role of the GDI will expand significantly, Alshaabani told Xinhua. "It will not only help developing countries address today's development challenges, but also help them build the capacity to adapt to future technological change." "In my view, this is one of the most promising transformations of the GDI: from development assistance to jointly building the capacity to develop. For the Global South, this capacity could become one of the most important resources of the next decade," said Gasimov.■

item.title: China urges Japan to stop any attempt at "remilitarization": spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- China urges Japan to deeply reflect on its history of aggression, heed the calls of regional countries and stop pursuing any attempt at "remilitarization," Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Monday. Guo made the remarks at a regular media briefing when asked about reports that the Russian Foreign Ministry had notified Japan over the U.S. deployment of the Typhon mid-range missile system in Kyushu, stressing that the deployment is unacceptable, urging Japan to fully recognize the outcomes of World War II and stop "remilitarization." "The Typhon mid-range missile system is a strategic offensive weapon, and Japan's introduction of the system is yet another piece of evidence of its accelerated 'remilitarization,'" Guo said. Guo said the move increases risks of military confrontation and an arms race, threatens strategic balance and regional stability, and undermines the legitimate security interests of neighboring countries. The international community is highly vigilant after the move, and people in multiple Asian countries have voiced opposition to it, Guo said. China has repeatedly lodged strong protests with Japan through diplomatic channels and recently sent a diplomatic note to the Japanese side to reiterate its solemn position, he added. ■

item.title: China, U.S. have candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges during consultations on economic and trade issues
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
NEW YORK, Sept. 20 (Xinhua) -- Chinese and U.S. teams on Sunday held candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges during consultations on economic and trade issues. Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng, who led the Chinese delegation, held economic and trade talks in New York with U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, head of the U.S. side, and U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer. Guided by the important consensus reached by the heads of state of the two countries, they have engaged in exchanges on important economic and trade issues of common concern, as well as the implementation of consensus reached in previous talks, by upholding the principles of mutual respect, peaceful coexistence and win-win cooperation. They also held dialogues on AI-related issues. ■

item.title: Xi replies to students from 10 U.S. universities
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping recently replied to students from 10 U.S. universities who wrote to him after attending youth exchanges in China. Xi noted that he was delighted to learn that the students enjoyed a pleasant and memorable journey in China. Xi said he was pleased to hear that the students expressed in the letter their appreciation for Chinese civilization, their hope for friendly cooperation between China and the United States, and their willingness to act as envoys of friendship bridging the Pacific Ocean. Young people from China and the United States, Xi said, share the same planet Earth and jointly shoulder the mission of the times. He expressed hope that the students would join the vast number of young people in both countries in striving to carry forward, uphold, and advance China-U.S. friendly cooperation, and work together to foster mutual understanding and affinity between the two peoples and to ensure the steady and long-term development of bilateral relations, so as to contribute the vitality of youth to building a better world. Recently, nearly 100 students from Harvard University and nine other U.S. universities wrote to Xi, sharing their experiences and what they had gained from the Future Makers 2026 China-U.S. Youth Tour for a Shared Asia-Pacific Future and other exchange events in China, and expressing their willingness to contribute to promoting China-U.S. friendship. ■

item.title: Xi to pay state visit to U.S. from Sept. 23 to 25
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping will pay a state visit to the United States from Sept. 23 to 25 at the invitation of U.S. President Donald Trump, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson announced on Monday. During the visit, Xi and Trump will have an in-depth exchange of views on major issues concerning China-U.S. relations and world peace and development, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said at a regular news briefing. Head-of-state diplomacy plays an irreplaceable role in providing strategic guidance for China-U.S. relations, and the exchange of visits between the two heads of state within six months marks a historic milestone, Guo said. China is ready to work with the U.S. side to enrich the connotation of the constructive relationship of strategic stability, enhance dialogue and cooperation, properly manage differences, and continuously contribute to the well-being of both peoples and global peace, stability and prosperity, he added. ■

item.title: CPC leadership meeting studies major issues on Party self-governance, sets dates for Party plenum
item.description:
Published: 2026-09-21
BEIJING, Sept. 21 (Xinhua) -- Xi Jinping, general secretary of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee, on Monday chaired a meeting of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee, which studied major issues on strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance and set the dates for an upcoming Party plenum in October. The meeting decided that the fifth plenary session of the 20th Central Committee of the CPC will be held from Oct. 26 to 29 in Beijing. The meeting also decided to submit a document on the CPC Central Committee's decision regarding strengthening full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance to the plenum for deliberation. An earlier draft of the decision was circulated among Party members and non-Party figures for comment, drawing broad support from those consulted. The meeting noted that the document provides an objective assessment of the achievements and experience in advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance in the new era, offers an in-depth analysis of the situation and tasks facing Party building in the present and coming period, and sets out strategic plans for continuing to advance full and rigorous Party self-governance. The meeting stressed that, to strengthen full and rigorous Party self-governance with perseverance, it is imperative to uphold the Party's overall leadership and the centralized, unified leadership of the CPC Central Committee, maintain a strict approach without wavering, and improve the systems for exercising full and rigorous self-governance. Efforts must be made to ensure that the Party remains a vibrant Marxist governing party that stays at the forefront of the times, enjoys the wholehearted support of the people, withstands all tests, and serves as the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, said the meeting. The meeting called for fully recognizing the significance and urgency of unswervingly advancing full and rigorous Party self-governance, adopting higher standards and taking more concrete measures to address the prominent issues facing Party building. Other matters were also discussed at the meeting. ■
